title: Nitric Acid and Halogens
topicTitle: Oxy-acids of nitrogen (name and formula); chemical properties of nitric acid; ring test for nitrate ion; halogens: general characteristics; comparative study of Cl2, Br2, I2; haloacids
notes: **Nitric acid preparation:** $3NaNO_3 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow NaHSO_4 + HNO_3$ ( laboratory ). Ostwald process industrially: $4NH_3 + 5O_2 \rightarrow 4NO + 6H_2O$, then $2NO + O_2 \rightarrow 2NO_2$, then $3NO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow 2HNO_3 + NO$.

**Properties of $HNO_3$:** strong acid, powerful oxidising agent. With metals: $Cu + 4HNO_3 \rightarrow Cu(NO_3)_2 + 2NO_2 + 2H_2O$ (concentrated); $3Cu + 8HNO_3 \rightarrow 3Cu(NO_3)_2 + 2NO + 4H_2O$ (dilute). Non-metals like C and S are oxidised to $CO_2$ and $H_2SO_4$.

**Ring test for nitrate:** add $FeSO_4$ then conc. $H_2SO_4$ carefully down the side. A brown ring at the interface confirms nitrate: $NO_3^- + 3Fe^{2+} + 4H^+ \rightarrow NO + 3Fe^{3+} + 2H_2O$; $NO + Fe^{2+} \rightarrow [Fe(NO)]^{2+}$ (brown).
**Halogen trend:** reactivity decreases down group: $F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2$. Bond dissociation energy decreases down group.
**Haloacids strength:** acid strength increases down group: $HF < HCl < HBr < HI$. Bond strength decreases down group, making proton donation easier.
